title: Honest Prediction for Always-Selected Units When Selected-Control Mass Vanishes
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < 7.4, salvageable=false. Independent validity confirms sound matching honest-length rate but narrow benchmark scope; accepted-bank comparison remains unrepaired.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a matching oracle-relative length rate for two-cell lotteries over fixed central intervals, with global coverage averaged over training, target, and report randomness. The clipped empirical mean argument supplies the logarithm-free upper bound, and the three-law certificate supplies the same-order neighborhood converse; the TL;DR does not leave its matching-rate claim unproved. The population ambiguity characterization is already established in [Lee (2026)](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.02898v2), so the contribution is statistical calibration and regret rather than new causal identification. The converse exploits the benchmark's deliberately saturated target-cell allocation and changes only control selection, so the support-contamination calculation does not establish a separate statistical difficulty or metric-dependent boundary. The binary partition, fixed score, and benchmark-specific local converse limit the result's general significance. The attaining rule reports full intervals whenever n gamma_n kappa_n is at most 10,000, and no delivered computation establishes useful finite-sample performance beyond that conservative guarantee; these constraints keep the projected paper score at 6.2. proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a logarithm-free matching oracle-relative honest-length rate for the declared weak-floor binary-cell Lee model, using clipped empirical calibration and an unrestricted three-law lower certificate. Independent math and citation checks pass, but the narrow benchmark scope and conservative attaining rule do not clear field novelty (incremental; score 6.2 versus 7.4). The accepted-bank prior-work comparison remains unrepaired; no Lean formalization, kernel verification, or reusable promotion was attempted.
tldr: The headline result is a matching minimax rate for globally honest randomized prediction of the treated outcome, translated into an effect report for an independent always-selected control. For \(a+b>0\), in both total-variation and Hellinger neighborhoods of radius \(M/\sqrt n\), excess expected length over the same-law compatible population oracle has order \(\min\{1,(n\gamma_n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}\}\). A nonnegative three-law certificate supplies the converse, and the observable mean-calibrated clipped allocation rule attains the rate with at least \(90\%\) finite-sample marginal coverage throughout the public-floor global class. No logarithmic factor is needed. The certified-band rule remains a conservative benchmark. The result settles the rate and consistency boundary; exact minimax constants, fixed-floor efficiency, conditional coverage, and empirical Job Corps applicability remain outside the headline.
gap: Full-observed Lee ambiguity is identified, but its population characterization does not determine how sparse calibration and unseen support mass jointly limit oracle-relative prediction length. Existing volume and selective-risk guarantees use other targets or relaxed oracles.
fill: The clipped subprobability formulation makes the nuisance cancellation explicit. Singular witnesses identify population phase changes; a globally valid count program yields an upper benchmark; finite three-law likelihood inequalities supply an unrestricted converse. The frontier question requires a matching observable construction rather than a grid optimization or an assumed limiting experiment.
